source.text: ወይቤለኒ፡ ኡርኤል፡ በዝየ፡ †ደሚሮሙ፡ መላእክት፡ ምስለ፡ አንስት፡ ይቀውሙ፡ ወመንፈስቲሆሙ፡ ብዙኃ፡ ራእየ፡ ከዊኖሙ፡ አርኰስዎሙ፡ ለሰብእ፡ ወያስሕትዎሙ፡ ከመ፡ ይሡዑ፡ ለአጋንንት፡ ከመ፡ አማልክት፡ እስከ፡ ዕለተ፡ ዐባይ፡ ኵነኔ፡ በዛ፡ ይትኴነኑ፡ እስከ፡ ይትፈጸሙ።

translation.text: Urel told me, “Here the angels who joined with women will stand.[a] Their spirits, taking many forms, defiled humankind and will lead them astray to sacrifice to demons as gods, until the great day of judgment, on which they will be judged until they are brought to an end.[b]”

footnotes.text: Urel follows the selected spelling ኡርኤል. The printed joining expression begins with a dagger, not a letter ተ; that critical sign is retained in the source rather than turned into a new verb prefix. The compressed joining construction is rendered conservatively, not claimed as a recovered earlier wording.

The selected text shifts from defiled to will lead astray, and both are retained. Taking many forms renders the appearance/form expression. Being brought to an end follows the completion verb; the verse does not explain a more exact mechanism of destruction.

translation.text: The wives of the erring angels will become “like peaceful ones.”[a]

footnotes.text: The quoted expression is corrupt, not an assured promise that these wives become peaceful. The selected Ethiopic literally has a dagger-marked phrase like peaceful ones. Dillmann1865 column323 discusses the peace/friendliness sense and cites19:2. Charles printed50 note49 calls the expression corrupt and discusses a different Greek sirens reading; that different wording is not silently substituted into this translation of the selected Ethiopic. The quoted English is a critical fragment, not a recovered coherent outcome.

translation.text: I, Henok, alone saw the vision—the ends of everything—and no one among humankind sees as I saw.[a]

footnotes.text: Henok follows the selected personal-name spelling. The source places the vision and the ends of everything in a compressed sequence, retained here without adding a claim about an ancient autograph or about what all people will see in the future.

translation.text: Urel, one of the holy angels—for he is concerned with the world and with “trembling.”[a]

footnotes.text: The list uses a short relation of the world and of trembling, introduced by for/because; concerned with supplies an English relation without adding a specific office or an unprinted appointment verb. The world expression is an editorial emendation in Charles printed52 note4. The noun trembling is enclosed by daggers; Dillmann1865 column312 gives that sense and explicitly cites20:2. Charles note5 suggests that the word may go back to a corrupt transliteration of Tartarus. This is his suggestion, not an independently verified name, and Tartarus is not silently substituted.

translation.text: Rufael, one of the holy angels, concerned with the spirits of humankind.[a]

footnotes.text: The source gives a bare of-the-spirits relation, not an explicit over or appointed verb in this unit. Concerned with keeps that relation broad. Rufael follows the selected name, not a supplied variant from another angel list.

translation.text: Raguel, one of the holy angels, who carries out vengeance concerning the world [and] the lights.[a]

footnotes.text: The conjunction and is bracketed in the selected edition; Charles printed52 note8 calls it an intrusion. The vengeance verb can express punishment or avenging on someone’s behalf. The source marks world and lights with ለ; concerning keeps that relation qualified instead of asserting a secure direction of vengeance. The world expression is not silently rewritten as the world of the luminaries.

translation.text: Mikael, one of the holy angels, for he was appointed over the best portion of humankind—over the people.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected verb is the passive appointed/commanded form ተአዘዘ, not the command-noun spelling suggested by raw OCR. Dillmann1865 column793 supports the appointed/commanded sense, and columns253–254 explicitly cite20:5 for the best-portion expression. The final source says the people; it does not name Israel here.

translation.text: Saraqael, one of the holy angels, who is over the spirits [those from the living],[a] who sin in spirit.[b]

footnotes.text: The bracketed words are marked as an intrusion in Charles printed52 note16. Those from the living is only a provisional rendering; the first bracketed form and the complete attachment require further review. The bracket is retained, not silently omitted.

Charles printed52 note17 asks whether the second spirit expression is an accusative of limitation or locative. In spirit follows the latter possibility without claiming it is the sole established construction. The unit remains provisional because of the bracketed wording and its relation to the surrounding clause.

translation.text: Gebriel, one of the holy angels, who is over the Garden, serpents and cherubim.[a]

footnotes.text: Gebriel follows the selected personal-name form. The serpent word is supported by Dillmann1865 column870, which explicitly cites20:7; it is not an added class from a different angel list. Cherubim translates the selected form Kiruben. No additional angel name or eighth numbered unit is supplied after this verse: the next selected heading is chapter21.
